passages.text: We truly tell you that on the day of judgment it will be more bearable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah than for you to remain in the place of disobedience. First, because you did not understand what is reasonable for yourselves; second, because, after hearing about us, you did not come to us; third, because you disobeyed us even when we came. Therefore, out of concern for you, we freely pray that our peace may come upon you. If you wish to have it, you must eagerly undertake not to do wrong and courageously bear being wronged. Human nature would not endure this unless it first gained knowledge of the surpassing benefit, which is to know the righteous nature of the one who surpasses everything: that, in avenging the wronged, he punishes, and that he benefits the reverent forever.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἢ τῷ τῆς ἀπειθείας τόπῳ ἐνδιατελεῖν
lexical_decisions.chosen: than for you to remain in the place of disobedience
lexical_decisions.rationale: The infinitive is read as remaining in the location designated by the dative, with the addressed listeners as its contextual subject. A rendering that treats the place itself as the object of judgment is also possible, but must still account for the expressed remaining infinitive rather than omit it.

lexical_decisions.chosen: in avenging the wronged, he punishes
lexical_decisions.rationale: The wronged are the object of the avenging participle. The finite verb's punished object is unexpressed; the main text does not make the wronged people the ones punished, and leaves the implied wrongdoers unnamed.
The term describes those practicing reverence or piety, with the divine referent supplied by the surrounding argument. It is not replaced by a denominational group name.

passages.text: Oh, God's great, wise hand, which does everything in all things! For he has brought into being a countless multitude of birds, a varied multitude in which each differs from another in every respect: colors, beaks, claws, looks, dispositions, sounds, and everything else. How many different forms of plants there are too, distinguished by countless colors, qualities, and scents! How many animals of the dry land and of the waters, whose shapes, forms, arrangements, colors, ways of life, dispositions, natures, and multitude cannot be recounted! And also the multitudes and heights of mountains, differences among stones, fearsome recesses, springs, rivers, lakes, seas, harbors, islands, forests, the whole inhabited world, and uninhabited places.

lexical_decisions.rationale: The same word is rendered consistently in the bird and animal lists. Opinions or judgments are lexical alternatives, but dispositions better describes the behavioral character attributed to these living creatures without removing their cognitive individuality.
The noun can mean the eyes' looks or expressions, or the act of looking. Looks preserves that range rather than specifying eye color or anatomical structure not named here.
The word can indicate placements, positions, or bodily arrangements. It is distinguished from the adjacent shapes and forms rather than collapsed into them.

passages.text: Thus Adam, made according to his likeness, is created blind, is handed over without knowledge of good or evil, is found a transgressor, is expelled from the garden, and is punished with death. Likewise, the one who fashioned him, since he does not see from every direction, says concerning Sodom's destruction, ‘Come, let us go down and see whether they are carrying things through according to the outcry from them that comes to me; if not, so that I may know.’ He thereby shows himself ignorant. As for saying about Adam, ‘Let us cast him out, lest he stretch out his hand, touch the tree of life, eat, and live forever,’ saying ‘lest’ shows ignorance; adding ‘lest he eat and live forever’ also shows envy. And the writing, ‘God reflected that he had made the human,’ shows both reconsideration and ignorance. For ‘reflected’ is deliberation, by which someone, through ignorance, wishes to determine precisely the outcome of what he wants, or the reflection of one regretting what did not turn out as intended. And the writing, ‘The Lord smelled a fragrant scent,’ belongs to one in need, while taking pleasure in the smoke from flesh does not belong to a good one. Testing too, as it is written, ‘The Lord tested Abraham,’ belongs to an evil one ignorant of the outcome of endurance.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: γνῶσιν ἀγαθοῦ ἢ κακοῦ οὐκ ἔχων παραδέδοται
lexical_decisions.chosen: is handed over without knowledge of good or evil
lexical_decisions.rationale: The passive handed over and the absence of knowledge are both retained. The clause does not name the recipient or purpose of the handing over, so none is supplied.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἰ κατὰ τὴν κραυγὴν αὐτῶν τὴν ἐρχομένην πρὸς μὲ συντελοῦνται
lexical_decisions.chosen: whether they are carrying things through according to the outcry from them that comes to me
lexical_decisions.rationale: The supplied verb concerns completion or carrying through, but does not expressly name the conduct being completed. The English retains that open expression rather than supplying the familiar wording from a different form of the scriptural quotation.

In the argument about God's reflected decision, metanoeo concerns reconsideration, not a moral-spiritual redirection toward God. The policy's contextual exception is therefore applied; the source's polemical accusation is retained without imposing a doctrine that resolves it.

The noun denotes the fatty smoke or smell associated with flesh being cooked or offered. The main text retains flesh and smoke without identifying a particular animal or adding a sacrificial procedure.

passages.text: In this way Simon seemed to show many things from the scriptures: that God is subject to every passion. Peter replied, ‘If an evil and thoroughly wicked person takes no pleasure in exposing himself for the things in which he sins, answer me.’ Simon said, ‘He takes no pleasure in it.’ Peter said, ‘How, then, can God be evil and wicked, if through his remnant the evil things written publicly against him were added?’ Simon said, ‘It is possible that the accusation against him was written by another power contrary to his intention.’ Peter said, ‘Then let us investigate this first. If he exposed himself by his own will, as you already agreed, he is not wicked. But if it was by another power, we must investigate and examine with all our strength whether someone accused him, though he alone is good, of all the evils.’

lexical_decisions.rationale: The supplied noun λείμμα denotes a remnant, remainder, or residue. His remnant is retained as a potentially collective agent rather than silently substituting a different noun meaning will or permission. Its exact referent is not established by this passage.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μή τις αὐτὸν μόνον ἀγαθὸν ὄντα ἐπὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς κακοῖς ὑπέβαλεν
lexical_decisions.chosen: whether someone accused him, though he alone is good, of all the evils
lexical_decisions.rationale: The verb can denote insinuating, falsely imputing, or bringing an accusation. The main reading preserves the possibility of another power's false charge and the explicit alone-good qualification without naming that power.

source_issues.issue: The printed remnant or residue noun is unusual in the argument about publicly written accusations. The English preserves its ordinary lexical meaning with the referent unresolved; it is not an emendation to an unprinted word for will. A collective remnant belonging to God is defensible, but that identification remains tentative.

passages.text: On the following day in Tyre, I came to the quiet place as we had agreed. I saw and greeted the others along with some additional people, but, not seeing Apion, I asked why he was absent. Someone said that he had been seriously unwell in body since the previous evening. When I said that it would be reasonable to set out at once and visit him, nearly everyone asked that I speak with them first; afterward I could visit him too. So, with everyone of one mind, I began to speak:

lexical_decisions.source_quote: δυσαρρώστως αὐτὸν ἀπ’ αὐτῆς ἑσπέρας ἐσχηκέναι τὸ σωμάτιον
lexical_decisions.chosen: he had been seriously unwell in body since the previous evening
lexical_decisions.rationale: The report concerns bodily illness. The diminutive body-form need not imply that Apion was small, weak, or a child; the English retains its bodily reference without adding a diagnosis.
